sentences.text: Revenue rose from $96.6 billion in FY2017 [F1] to $332 billion in FY2026 [F10], a 14.7% compound rate [F221].
Operating margin widened from 30.1% in FY2017 [F41] to 46.8% in FY2026 [F50], the window high [D974].
Part of the 4.6pp operating margin rise in FY2021 [D220] came from gross margin gains that the filing credits partly to a change in server and network equipment useful lives [P51][P53].
Revenue growth accelerated to 17.8% in FY2026 [D472] from 14.9% in FY2025 [D418].
Intelligent Cloud added 11.2pp of the 17.8% FY2026 revenue growth [D917][D472].
Productivity and Business Processes added 6.8pp [D892], while More Personal Computing subtracted 0.2pp [D942].
The filing ties the FY2026 revenue increase to Microsoft Cloud [P17], which contributed 16.2pp [D568] and 64.6% of revenue [D566].
Operating expenses grew 7.4% [D491] against 17.8% revenue growth [D472], giving an incremental operating margin of 53.3% [D498].
Diluted EPS rose 31.6% [D476], close to net income growth of 31.3% [D474], as diluted shares fell 0.2% [D493].
Operating margin of 46.8% [F50] sits 5.1pp above its 41.7% window median [D975].
Gross margin fell 0.9pp to 67.9% [D486][F30]; cost of revenue, up 21.1% [D489], cut 0.9pp from operating margin [D500].
The filing attributes the Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage decline to AI infrastructure investment and sales mix shift to Azure [P11][D486].
Net margin of 40.3% [F70] sits 6.5pp below operating margin [F50], as a 19.4% tax rate [D458] took $32.2 billion [X114].
Other income swung to $10.7 billion [X124] from a $4.9 billion loss [X123], mainly from $6.5 billion of OpenAI gains [P7].
Operating cash flow rose 34.4% to $183 billion [D477][F100], but free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion [D478][F120].
The filing attributes the rise in cash used in investing mainly to a $51.4 billion increase in property additions [P1], taking capital expenditure to $116 billion, up 79.6% [F110][D479].
Free cash flow was 0.50x net income [D460], the window low [D988], against a 0.91x window median [D990].
Capital expenditure at 34.9% of revenue [D455] and 3.38x D&A [D461] now limits cash conversion more than earnings do.
Net cash of $72.9 billion [D465], 22.0% of revenue [D466], ranks at the 83rd percentile of six software peers [D1006]; the peer median is -7.2% [D1007].
Net cash has risen from $38.5 billion in FY2024 [D357].
The current ratio of 1.23x [F200] is the window low [D991], against a 1.93x median [D993].
Buybacks and dividends totalled $48.7 billion [D467], 72.7% of free cash flow [D468]; diluted shares fell only 0.2% [D493].
Free cash flow was 0.70x net income in FY2025 [D406].
It fell further to 0.50x in FY2026 [D460], a medium-severity pattern across two years [R1].
The filing attributes the rise in cash used in investing mainly to a $51.4 billion increase in property additions [P1][F110].
Other income of $10.7 billion [X124] includes $6.5 billion of OpenAI gains [P7], so part of net income growth is non-operating and may not repeat.
Product revenue members overlap, so product totals are not summed here; segment and geography figures carry the driver analysis.
Free cash flow to net income staying near the 0.50x window low [D460][D988] in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the squeeze; recovery toward the 0.91x median [D990] would reverse it.
If other income falls from $10.7 billion [X124] back toward the FY2025 loss of $4.9 billion [X123], net margin of 40.3% [F70] would lose investment-gain support, visible in the FY2027 10-K.
Operating margin holding at the 46.8% high [F50][D974] would confirm the margin trend; a fall toward the 41.7% median [D975] would reverse it.
